correctness.rationale: The explicit 28 lines are distinct bitangents in each odd characteristic. All 3276 triple-line determinants were computed exactly in Z[zeta_8], with precisely 60 zeros and all nonzero norm prime factors confined to 2,3,5,17, establishing generic stability. The p=3,5,17 finite-field incidences are complete cross-product computations in F_{p^2}, not partial samples. The Frobenius fixed-point spectra are exact permutations of generic cyclotomic intersection classes. The characteristic-five count of all 31 rational projective points has an additional direct combinatorial explanation. Pair multiplicity checks equal C(28,2)=378 in every stratum. A standalone standard-library verifier reproduces the computational steps.

value.rationale: The exact list of exceptional primes for a canonical 28-line configuration answers a natural good-reduction problem, and the Frobenius fixed-point spectrum describes all rational singularities of its reduction. The p=5 result is a geometrically meaningful complete finite-projective-plane incidence phenomenon, not an arbitrary small computation: all 31 F5-points become triple or quadruple points while the Fermat quartic itself has no F5-points. The novelty is not the elementary rationality of the 28 lines or the known characteristic-zero basket.
